### Machine vision

| Scenario | Method | Result | Key metrics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orchard — stereo camera (ZED X): YOLO detection + ByteTrack + 3D positions | `yolov8s + bytetrack + depth_centroid` | **pass** | precision 99 % ✓<br>recall (objects ≥ 10 px) 71 % ✓<br>3D position error 24 mm ✓<br>tracked ids in last frame 39 ✓<br>targets created 39 pairs ✓ |

<details><summary><code>ctl_petri_deadlock</code> — Petri net: siphon → deadlock → GMEC monitor (chapter 4)</summary>

Two processes acquire the robot and the zone in opposite orders. Reachability finds the deadlock; the siphon {rM, rZ, a2, b2} empties; one monitor place (a1 + b1 ≤ 1) restores liveness; the S³PR builder reproduces the same net.

*How to reproduce:* Control › Course examples… → pick the document → Analyse (Control tab shows the report and the graph).

| Metric | Value | Criterion |

| max-plus cycle | 32 s | 32 s ✓ |

</details>

<details><summary><code>grp_architectures</code> — Architectures: the same mission centralised, decentralised and hybrid — coordinator outage, robot failure, partition (chapter 3)</summary>

A five-phase mission (formation, move, task allocation, gathering, return) with a robot failure at 40 s and a coordinator outage 60–110 s runs under the three architectures of chapter 3: the centralised group stalls while its coordinator is down, the decentralised group never depends on it (but takes slots by index and needs agreement time), the hybrid group plans globally, keeps the formation locally and falls back during the outage. A second document puts robots beyond the coordinator's range (radio 3.5 m with 20 % loss, coordinator 3 m); a third runs on configured station robots with zones, a no-go pillar, a des supervisor and a mode automaton.
